description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern dish featuring a whole slow-roasted lamb, often stuffed with aromatic rice, nuts, and spices. This celebratory meal promises incredibly tender, fall-off-the-bone meat infused with rich, complex flavors. Perfect for special occasions, it creates an unforgettable centerpiece that embodies the generous spirit of Middle Eastern hospitality.

ingredients.item: Whole lamb leg or shoulder, bone-in

ingredients.notes: mixture of allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb Marinade
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine yogurt, minced garlic, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon Ouzi spice mix, 1 tablespoon salt, and 1/2 tablespoon black pepper. Score the lamb all over with a sharp knife and generously rub the marinade into the lamb, ensuring it penetrates the scores. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice Stuffing Base
instructions.text: Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear. In a large pot or deep skillet, heat 2 tablespoons ghee or olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the lamb mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until it is thoroughly browned. Drain any excess fat.

instructions.title: Season and Partially Cook the Stuffing
instructions.text: Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon Ouzi spice mix, 1 tablespoon salt, and 1/2 tablespoon black pepper into the lamb mince and onion mixture. Add the rinsed basmati rice and stir well to coat all the grains. Pour in 4 cups of water or lamb broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is partially cooked and most of the liquid is absorbed. Stir in the toasted pine nuts and slivered almonds.

instructions.title: Stuff and Truss the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Carefully remove the marinated lamb from the refrigerator. Gently stuff the partially cooked rice mixture into the cavity of the lamb leg or shoulder. If necessary, use kitchen twine to truss the lamb to secure the stuffing inside and maintain the lamb's shape during roasting. Place the stuffed lamb in a large, sturdy roasting pan.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb to Perfection
instructions.text: Add 1-2 cups of water or broth to the bottom of the roasting pan. This helps to prevent the lamb from drying out and creates a moist environment for slow roasting. Cover the roasting pan tightly with heavy-duty aluminum foil. Roast in the preheated oven for 4-5 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. For the last 30 minutes of cooking, remove the foil to allow the skin to crisp slightly and achieve a beautiful golden-brown color.

instructions.title: Rest, Garnish, and Serve
instructions.text: Once roasted, carefully remove the lamb from the oven and transfer it to a large carving board or serving platter. Cover it loosely with foil and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. This crucial resting period allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring maximum tenderness and flavor. Garnish generously with fresh mint leaves and chopped parsley before serving. Serve the tender lamb with the aromatic rice stuffing.

tips: To ensure the lamb is incredibly tender, marinate it overnight. The yogurt helps break down the fibers, resulting in a more succulent roast.
For an extra layer of flavor, toast the nuts for the stuffing until golden brown before adding them. This enhances their aroma and crunch.
Always allow the roasted lamb to rest for at least 20-30 minutes after cooking. This step is crucial for juicy, tender meat as it allows the internal juices to redistribute.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East with a dish that epitomizes celebration and hospitality: Lamb Ouzi, whole slow roasted. This isn't just a meal; it's an event, a magnificent centerpiece destined to impress at any special gathering. Imagine the intoxicating aroma filling your home as a beautifully spiced, tender whole lamb, brimming with aromatic rice, nuts, and dried fruits, slowly roasts to perfection. While it may seem daunting, the process of preparing a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is surprisingly rewarding, offering an unforgettable feast that speaks volumes of tradition and flavor. Get ready to transform your kitchen into a hub of Middle Eastern delight and bring this incredible dinner recipe to life.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?
Lamb Ouzi, often spelled Qouzi or Ghozi, is a renowned Middle Eastern dish, particularly popular in Iraq, Syria, Jordan, and the Gulf countries. At its core, Ouzi refers to a celebratory preparation of lamb, typically slow-cooked until incredibly tender, and traditionally served with a rich, spiced rice pilaf often studded with nuts and dried fruits. While smaller cuts like lamb shanks or shoulders are frequently used for daily meals or smaller gatherings, the truly grand version, and the one we're focusing on, involves a whole lamb or a significant portion of it, roasted low and slow. This method ensures the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender, infused with deep flavors, and makes for a breathtaking presentation. It's a dish reserved for weddings, Eid celebrations, and significant family feasts, symbolizing abundance and generosity.

## Ingredients You'll Need
To create this spectacular whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi, you'll need a combination of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices:

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole lamb (approx. 20-30 lbs), cleaned and prepared by your butcher (ask for the inner cavity to be cleaned and neck/tail removed if preferred)
*   1/2 cup olive oil
*   1/4 cup lemon juice
*   1/4 cup apple cider vinegar
*   1/4 cup plain yogurt (optional, for tenderizing)
*   6-8 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 large onions, roughly chopped
*   2 tablespoons ground cumin
*   2 tablespoons ground coriander
*   1 tablespoon ground turmeric
*   1 tablespoon ground cinnamon
*   1 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1 teaspoon ground cloves
*   1 teaspoon black pepper
*   Salt to taste (generous amount)

For the Rice Stuffing:
*   4 cups Basmati rice, rinsed
*   1/2 cup olive oil
*   2 large onions, finely chopped
*   4-6 cloves garlic, minced
*   1/2 cup slivered almonds, toasted
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1/2 cup dried cranberries or raisins (optional)
*   2 tablespoons Lamb Ouzi spice blend (or a mix of 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp cardamom, 1/2 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp nutmeg)
*   8 cups lamb or chicken broth
*   Salt and pepper to taste

## Step-by-Step Instructions

1.  **Prepare the Lamb Marinade:** In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, yogurt (if using), minced garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, black pepper, and a generous amount of salt.
2.  **Marinate the Lamb:** Pat the whole lamb dry with paper towels. Rub the marinade all over the lamb, both inside the cavity and generously on the outside. Massage it into the skin. If possible, cover the lamb and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate deeply.
3.  **Pre-roast the Lamb (Optional but Recommended):** If your roasting pan allows, briefly brown the lamb on all sides in a very hot oven (400°F / 200°C) for 30-45 minutes. This helps develop a beautiful crust. Then reduce the oven temperature.
4.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large, sturdy roasting pan, preferably on a rack. Add about 2-3 cups of water or broth to the bottom of the pan to create steam and keep the lamb moist. Cover the entire pan tightly with foil or a roasting bag. Roast for 6-8 hours, or until the meat is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. For the last hour, remove the foil to allow the skin to crisp up.
5.  **Prepare the Rice Stuffing:** While the lamb is roasting (about 1.5-2 hours before it's done), heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onions until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
6.  **Cook the Rice:** Add the rinsed Basmati rice to the pot, along with the Lamb Ouzi spice blend, salt, and pepper. Stir well to coat the rice. Pour in the lamb or chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
7.  **Finish the Stuffing:** Gently fluff the cooked rice with a fork. Stir in the toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and dried cranberries/raisins (if using).
8.  **Assemble and Serve:** Carefully remove the whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi from the oven and let it rest, loosely tented with foil, for at least 30 minutes before carving. This is crucial for juicy meat. To serve, traditionally, the lamb is presented whole on a very large platter, surrounded by or generously stuffed with the aromatic rice pilaf. You can also carve the lamb into large pieces and arrange them artfully over the rice.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Source Quality Lamb:** The success of your Lamb Ouzi begins with the quality of your meat. Seek out fresh, high-quality lamb from a reputable butcher. A younger lamb will be more tender.
*   **Don't Skimp on Marination:** The longer the lamb marinates, the deeper and more complex its flavor will be. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
*   **Low and Slow is Key:** Resist the temptation to rush the roasting process. A low oven temperature over many hours is what breaks down the tough fibers, rendering the meat incredibly tender and succulent.
*   **Rest the Lamb:** After roasting, always allow the lamb to rest for at least 30 minutes (or even an hour for a whole lamb) before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, resulting in a more flavorful and moist bite.
*   **Toast Your Nuts:** Lightly toasting the slivered almonds and pine nuts brings out their nutty flavor and adds an extra layer of texture to the rice stuffing.
*   **Adjust Spices to Taste:** The spice blend is a guideline. Feel free to adjust the ratios of cinnamon, cardamom, and other spices to suit your personal preference. Some prefer a more pronounced cardamom, others more cinnamon.

## Serving Suggestions
The grandeur of whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi calls for equally delicious, yet complementary, accompaniments. A dollop of cool, creamy labneh (strained yogurt) or a simple cucumber-yogurt sauce offers a refreshing contrast to the rich lamb. Fresh, vibrant salads like Fattoush or Tabbouleh provide a burst of acidity and freshness, cutting through the richness. Pickled vegetables, such as turnips or cucumbers, are also fantastic for adding a tangy crunch. Warm pita bread or other Middle Eastern flatbreads are perfect for scooping up the flavorful rice and tender pieces of lamb. For a truly authentic experience, serve the Lamb Ouzi family-style on a large platter, allowing everyone to share in the magnificent feast.

## Variations & Substitutions
While the whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is a showstopper, there are ways to adapt this recipe to different preferences or practicalities:

*   **Meat Cuts:** If a whole lamb is too much or unavailable, you can achieve a similar flavor profile with a large lamb shoulder, leg of lamb, or even lamb shanks. Adjust roasting times accordingly.
*   **Rice Fillings:** Experiment with the nuts and dried fruits in your rice. Walnuts, pistachios, or even cashews can replace or supplement almonds and pine nuts. Dried apricots or dates can be used instead of cranberries or raisins for a different sweetness.
*   **Spices:** While a traditional Lamb Ouzi spice blend is ideal, you can create your own by adjusting quantities of cinnamon, cardamom, allspice, nutmeg, and a hint of white pepper. Some recipes also include a touch of ginger or dried rose petals for added aroma.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** For a heartier stuffing, some recipes include finely diced carrots, peas, or chickpeas mixed into the rice.
*   **Smoking:** For an even deeper flavor, if you have access to a large smoker, you can smoke the lamb for a few hours before transferring it to the oven to finish roasting.

Preparing a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is an unforgettable culinary adventure that culminates in a truly spectacular meal. It’s a dish that embodies warmth, generosity, and the rich flavors of Middle Eastern cuisine. The effort put into this magnificent dinner recipe is repaid manifold by the "oohs" and "aahs" of your guests and the sheer delight of savoring such tender, aromatic lamb. So, gather your ingredients, clear your schedule, and prepare to create a feast that will be talked about for years to come.
